items.title: Ramadan - Purpose of Fasting
items.excerpt: Aljazi Alsowaidi (6C) reports on the purpose of Ramadan.
items.body:
As Muslims, we celebrate Ramadan every year. Ramadan is the holy month of the Quran. In this month, good deeds are rewarded more. Allah gives us this special month to do more good things.

During Ramadan, we try to finish reading the whole Quran at least two times. We also make sure we pray the five daily prayers and Taraweeh prayer, which we only pray in Ramadan.

Ramadan is also special because we fast for thirty days. We fast from Fajr (around 4:00 a.m.) until Maghrib (approximately 6:00 p.m.). This means we do not eat or drink during this time.

Ramadan teaches us patience, kindness, and gratitude.
items.author: Aljazi Abdulla Alsowaidi (6C)

items.title: World Diabetes Day
items.excerpt: Diabetes affects millions of people worldwide. Understanding the disease and making healthy choices can help us protect ourselves and support those around us.
items.body:
World Diabetes Day falls on November 14th and has several objectives, including raising awareness about the seriousness of diabetes and its global prevalence; encouraging early screening; sharing information about prevention methods; and supporting patients and explaining the importance of regular treatment.

The official symbol of World Diabetes Day is the blue circle, representing global solidarity against diabetes and hope for improving the lives of those living with the disease. We can show our solidarity by wearing blue, getting tested for diabetes, and encouraging others to exercise and eat healthily.
items.author: Haya Hamad Al-hamar (6A)

items.title: What is Kindness?
items.excerpt: Grade 6 students explain what kindness means and how we can show it.
items.body:
What is kindness? Our Grade 6 students answered this question in their own words and pictures.

Shaikha shows us how to be KIND: know and use manners, include everyone, say no to bullying, and donate to charity. Dana explains that kindness means acting in a kind, compassionate and generous way. Sara tells the story of a hurt kitten she helped, and Talia lists five simple ways to be kind to others.
items.author: Grade 6 Students

items.title: What is Cooperation?
items.excerpt: Cooperation is a beautiful value that helps us succeed in life.
items.body:
Cooperation is a beautiful value that helps us succeed in life. It means working together and helping one another to reach a common goal. When we cooperate, we learn teamwork, kindness, and respect.

At school, cooperation makes learning more fun and easier. Students can help each other in class, share ideas, and work together on projects. When we cooperate with our teachers and classmates, our school becomes a happy and organized place.

Cooperation also teaches us to care for others and to be responsible. By working together at home, in school, and in our community, we can make the world a better place.

With cooperation, we grow stronger and achieve more!
items.author: Aisha Abulrahman Almarwani (5C)

items.title: Qatar's Beauty
items.excerpt: Maryam Almohannadi shares a poem to celebrate our lovely Qatar's National Day!
items.body:
In the desert sands so wide,
Qatar stands with pride.
Golden dunes under the blue sky,
A place where dreams can fly.

Busy markets full of color and light,
The Corniche is so calm and bright.
The call to prayer in the morning air,
In Qatar, traditions are everywhere.

The Pearl shines in the sun's glow,
A sign of progress, watch it grow.
In Katara, art and stories thrive,
Qatar's culture is alive.

Aspire Park, so green and neat,
A peaceful place, so sweet.
Qatar's spirit, strong and true,
In every heart, it shines through.

With each sunrise, a new day starts,
In Qatar, hope fills our hearts.
A land of dreams, where the future gleams,
Qatar, a place of hope and dreams.

In every smile, warm and true,
In a place I call home, Qatar.
items.author: Maryam Almohannadi (6A)

items.title: World Children's Day Celebration
items.excerpt: A report on how Albayan students celebrated World Children's Day with joy, activities, and reflection on children's rights around the world.
items.body:
World Children's Day is celebrated every year on November 20th. It's a day to celebrate children — their rights, their voices, and their dreams.

At Albayan, we celebrated with a full day of activities. Students created posters about children's rights, wore colorful clothes, and participated in games and performances.

In the morning assembly, we learned about children around the world who face difficult challenges. We discussed what we can do to help — even in small ways.

The day reminded us that every child deserves love, safety, education, and a chance to dream. And that we are lucky to have all of these — and to be able to share them with others.
items.author: Haya Alhamar

items.title: School Trip to Qatar Scouts and Guides
items.excerpt: An account of our memorable visit to the Qatar Scouts and Guides, where students learned outdoor skills, teamwork, and the spirit of scouting.
items.body:
Last month, our class went on an exciting trip to the Qatar Scouts and Guides center. It was a day full of learning, teamwork, and fun.

When we arrived, our guide showed us around the camp. We learned how to pitch a tent, tie different types of knots, and read a compass. We even learned how to make a small fire safely (with teacher supervision, of course).

The best part was the teamwork activities. We had to cross an imaginary river using only a few planks of wood — and we had to work together. It showed us that success comes from cooperation.

By the end of the day, we were tired but happy. The trip reminded us that learning doesn't only happen in classrooms.
items.author: Maria Abdulaziz

items.title: Teacher's Day Report
items.excerpt: A tribute to our wonderful teachers at Albayan, capturing the celebrations, thank-yous, and heartfelt moments of World Teacher's Day.
items.body:
World Teacher's Day is a special day to thank our teachers for everything they do. At Albayan, we celebrated with a full day of surprises.

In the morning, students greeted teachers with flowers and cards. Some classes prepared songs and poems. Others wrote heartfelt thank-you letters.

Our teachers work so hard to help us learn and grow. They wake up early, prepare lessons, grade homework, and most importantly, they believe in us.

So on World Teacher's Day — and every day — we say thank you. Thank you for teaching us, guiding us, and making our school a happy place.
items.author: Badriya, Shahd, Dhabia
